critical_steps: The critical equality forces the singleton mass to be positive, contradicting any zero-measure set containing that atom.
The erased frame operator is S minus the atomic rank-one contribution.
Conjugation by S^{-1/2} reduces invertibility to I minus a rank-one operator with eigenvalue 1-ell.
At ell=1, S^{-1}F(omega_0) is an explicit nonzero kernel vector.
The source proof only shows the exceptional support outside the atom is null; the atom itself has positive mass.
integrity.proof_basis: Exact rank-one factorization of the erased continuous-frame operator.
integrity.unproved_limits: No weakest formula for multi-atom or arbitrary measurable erasure is claimed.

scientific_limitations: The result classifies singleton erasure for the canonical leverage parameter, not arbitrary measurable or multiple erasures.
The continuous-frame conclusion is about preservation of the lower frame bound; pointwise completeness can be altered on null sets.

title: Critical atomic leverage exactly controls singleton erasure for continuous frames
